Release notes (vendor firmware)

Search Fortinet's known and resolved issues for FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate firmware, compare two versions before an upgrade, and read the release-note prose — from a corpus SATOM imports from signed packs.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view users.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate ADOM → Top bar → Tools (wrench) → Release Notes

What is it?#

Release Notes is a window for Fortinet's own release notes of the appliance firmware — FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate, matching the ADOM you are in. It lists known and resolved issues across versions, tells you what a move from one version to another resolves and what stays known, and lets you search the release-note text.

Since SATOM 3.0 the corpus comes only from signed packs: the API pack that ships with each release, and the rolling knowledge pack fetched from the knowledge feed or uploaded by hand (Knowledge packs). SATOM itself no longer contacts any vendor documentation site.

ℹ️Note

This is not SATOM's own changelog. For what changed in SATOM itself, see Software update; the version you run is printed in the footer of every page.

What does it do?#

Three tabs:

Tab What it answers
Issues Every known and resolved issue, filterable by version, status (Known / Resolved), topic and free text (bug id, description, workaround)
Upgrade advisor Pick Current: and → Target:, click Show advisory: the issues the move resolves, the issues still known in the target, and the relevant upgrade notes
Notes The prose sections of a release (for example what's new and upgrade notes), by version and section, with search

The Upgrade advisor tab can also show Upgrade Advisory verdicts above the bug diff — rule-based checks of the upgrade notes that flag what could stop the maintenance window. The Upgrade Advisory is available while Path Diagnostics is switched on (Settings → Path Diagnostics); it has no switch of its own.

ℹ️Note

Renamed on 2026-10-14: the release-notes reviewer was shown as Scout / Scout advisory until then. Scout is now the AI assistant, and the switch in this window is labelled Path Diagnostics (includes the Upgrade Advisory), because that is the switch it actually uses.

Above the tabs the window says where its knowledge comes from: Knowledge from <pack> (<date>), with the pack's age and a stale badge when it is older than 30 days. With no pack imported it says no knowledge pack imported on this node yet. The Upgrade Advisory and the Migration report show the same line.

Two buttons in the window header:

  • Reload corpus — re-reads the corpus from disk and reports how many issues and sections it holds and when it was written. Useful right after a pack import.
  • Knowledge packs… (administrators) — opens Software Update → Knowledge packs, where the feed is checked and packs are imported.

Requirements#

  • You are in the FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate ADOM. The menu entry is not offered in Global.
  • An imported pack. A fresh installation imports the release's API pack; the knowledge pack arrives from the feed (online) or by upload (air-gapped).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the window, use the three tabs, Reload corpus Read access — any view permission, for example monitoring.view
Knowledge packs… (and everything on that card) users.manage
Switch Path Diagnostics (includes the Upgrade Advisory) on or off users.manage (the switch is disabled for others)

How to use#

Find a known issue#

  1. In the product's ADOM, open Tools → Release Notes.
  2. On Issues, pick a version and/or status, or type in Search bug id / description / workaround ….
  3. Read Version, Status, Bug ID, Topic and Description.

The version pickers also list the builds your appliances of this product run, marked as having no notes here, when the corpus lacks them.

Plan an upgrade#

  1. Open Upgrade advisor.
  2. Choose Current: and → Target: versions (they must differ).
  3. Click Show advisory.
  4. Read the Upgrade Advisory verdicts (if Path Diagnostics is on), then the resolved issues, the issues still known in the target, and the notes.

Get newer notes (administrator)#

  1. Click Knowledge packs….
  2. On the Knowledge packs card, click Check now, then Import.
  3. Back in the window, click Reload corpus.

On an air-gapped network, upload the knowledge pack instead (Knowledge packs).

Example#

🧪Example — Before a FortiWeb maintenance window

You run 7.6.2 and plan 7.6.4. In Upgrade advisor, Current 7.6.2, Target 7.6.4, Show advisory: the list shows the issues fixed between the two and the issues still open in 7.6.4, followed by the upgrade notes for that release. The line above the tabs reads Knowledge from satom-apipack-kb-20261008 (2026-10-08), so the advice is current.

Result#

  • Nothing is written by reading. Reload corpus is recorded in the audit log as release_notes.reload; the Path Diagnostics switch as scout.switch.
  • A pack import merges its release notes into the corpus on this node. In a high-availability pair, import on the primary; the standby receives the corpus through data replication.

Troubleshooting#

"No release notes for this build in the local corpus — import a newer knowledge pack (Software Update → Knowledge packs)."#

Possible causes - No imported pack carries notes for that build yet (a very new build, or a node whose knowledge pack is old).

Solution 1. An administrator imports the newest knowledge pack (Knowledge packs). 2. Click Reload corpus.

Verification - The window lists the build's issues.

"No corpus on this node yet — import a knowledge pack (Software Update → Knowledge packs). It is not fetched from git."#

Possible causes - No pack with release notes was imported on this node (for example the installer's pack import was skipped).

Solution 1. Import the release's own pack (sudo satom execute apipack import shipped --yes) or a knowledge pack.

The knowledge line shows "stale"#

Possible causes - The newest knowledge pack on this node is older than 30 days: the daily fetch is off, failing, or the node is air-gapped.

Solution 1. Check Software Update → Knowledge packs → Last check. 2. Import a newer pack.

The advisory says sections "were not read"#

Possible causes - The corpus lacks a section the advisory needs for a version in the range.

Solution 1. Import a newer knowledge pack and ask again. The advisory is never called clean while coverage is missing.

"Pick a current and a target version." / "Pick two different versions."#

Possible causes - One version is missing, or both are the same.

"Turn on Path Diagnostics in Settings → Path Diagnostics to see the Upgrade Advisory."#

Possible causes - Path Diagnostics is switched off for the site, and the Upgrade Advisory follows that switch.

Solution 1. A user with users.manage ticks Path Diagnostics (includes the Upgrade Advisory) in this window, or switches on Path Diagnostics is available in Settings → Path Diagnostics → Settings (Path Diagnostics settings).

Verification - The window shows the toast Path Diagnostics on: the Upgrade Advisory is available. and Show advisory returns verdicts again.

Where is "Scan from Fortinet"?#

Removed in SATOM 3.0, together with version discovery and its routes. Crawling the vendor documentation is done only by the SATOM team's separate Knowledge Harvester; its result reaches you as packs. If you kept outbound access to the vendor documentation site only for SATOM, it is no longer needed.

Advanced#

Advanced Scope, storage and corrections

Every product's rows are stored in one corpus file, tagged per product; every read is filtered to the ADOM you are in. A pack import adds the versions the node does not hold, and replaces a version an earlier pack wrote when a pack built from a newer snapshot carries a different copy — that is how corrections arrive. A version this node scanned itself before 3.0 is local data and is never replaced. Which pack wrote each version is recorded with the corpus. The corpus is local to each node and is not stored in git.
